title: What is known about 1RB0RF_0LC---_1LD1LC_1RE0LA_1RA1RD_0RD1RF
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RF_0LC---_1LD1LC_1RE0LA_1RA1RD_0RD1RF.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Sweeps back and forth, each sweep rewriting the whole tape into its other form (011 to 100, 10 to 11, a period-12 word to its partner); a period-3 zone at the left end, then a few huge blocks of longer words (12, 15, 30 cells) that are built up and eaten in turn, and a short tail on the right; a halt needs a rightward sweep to meet 0001. Lean proves the sweep rules over the background words and the only local pattern that leads to a halt; no halt in 109 steps of the plain simulator, none in 3·1013 steps of an accelerated one (not verified).

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (B1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 46,120 cells have been visited and 27,671 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: sqrt/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.471). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.505).

claims.title: The sweeps cross the background words whole
claims.text: 9 shift rules: for every n and every surrounding tape, a sweep in the stated state crosses n copies of a background word and leaves n copies of its partner, in the stated number of steps (for example L D> (011)^n R ⟶ L (100)^n D> R).

claims.title: The only way to a halt
claims.text: The machine halts only when B reads a 1, and the only way there is D reading 0 0 0 1 (D, E and A each write a 1 and step right, and B meets the 1.

claims.title: The near misses are all at the right end
claims.text: In the first 109 steps the state that leads to the halt reads 0 0 0 6,026 times, every time on blank cells past the right end of the tape.

claims.title: Same table as its twin
claims.text: 1RB1RE_1RC0RF_0LD---_1LE1LD_1RA0LB_0RE1RF is this table with the states renamed (A→B, B→C, C→D, D→E, E→A, F→F); it starts in the state this machine calls E. The two runs from blank tape are different (no common configuration at the left end in their first 300,000 steps), but they use the same sweeps, words and halting pattern, and every rule here holds there after renaming.

claims.title: What the tape looks like
claims.text: Seen at the left end the tape is a clean zone (011)a (or (101)a), then a block of the period-12 word (101011010110)B that grows by one copy per visit of the left end, then one or two more huge blocks of longer words and a short tail such as (10)a 1 (10)b 1 and (110)3 (10)3, where the irregular events happen. The clean zone does not grow: it shrinks at each conversion of the left block. In the rightward form the soup reads as runs of 1s separated by 0 0.

claims.title: The accelerated simulator agrees with the plain one
claims.text: At 20 arrivals at the left end between 1.5·109 and 3.0·1010 steps (the later ones after six cycle-rule jumps) the accelerated simulator and the plain C simulator c/at.c give the same state, head position, tape and step count.

claims.title: A tail cycle, proved for all block sizes
claims.text: In the phase from 2.5·108 to 2.3·109 steps the tail repeats every 118 visits of the left end (B + 118, C − 25 words of the period-15 block per cycle; 5,250 re-occurrences in the plain run). One symbolic run of the accelerated simulator with the three big counts free proves the rule (a, B, C) = (42 + 3x0, 748 + 3x1, 190 + 3x2) → (a, B + 354, C − 75) in 708 events for all x ≥ 0; the plain engine confirms it on numbers. The run to 3·1013 steps found and used 17 other rules of this kind (15 of 6 events: B + 3 and a block 1^n − 18; 2 of 498 events: B + 249 and a period-30 block − 24), all 17 re-checked on numbers.

claims.title: No halt in the first 3·10<sup>13</sup> steps (accelerated run)
claims.text: The accelerated simulator runs 30,000,000,585,416 steps from blank tape without a halt (1,568,417 arrivals at the left end; 17 cycle rules, each proved by a symbolic run with its counts free and re-checked on numbers). The tool is not verified; it agrees with the plain simulator at 20 of 20 checkpoints up to 3.0·10<sup>10</sup> steps.

claims.title: Blocks and phases; why the closed-set recipe does not apply yet
claims.text: At arrivals at the left end the tape is 0 (011)^a 101101 (101011010110)^B junk (U)^C tail with B, C huge and U a word of 15, 21, 24 or 30 cells: the shape of the solved machines of this group. But there are phases with three big blocks, conversions of the whole left block, phases with a row of blocks (10)^k, k doubling from block to block (their number grows like the logarithm of the tape), the clean zone (011)^a is a third counter that shrinks at conversions, and the tails do not always cycle. Observed in plain runs to 6·1010 steps and accelerated runs beyond.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. Inside the tape, separators of two 0s are common in the rightward form, so a third 0 next to them is the danger. The run never produced one in 10<sup>9</sup> steps, but no invariant that forbids it is known.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows yet. Sweeps back and forth, each sweep rewriting the whole tape into its other form (011 to 100, 10 to 11, a period-12 word to its partner); a period-3 zone at the left end, then a few huge blocks of longer words (12, 15, 30 cells) that are built up and eaten in turn, and a short tail on the right; a halt needs a rightward sweep to meet 0001. This page runs the real machine, explains its sweeps and the words they rewrite, and lists what is proved.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 46,120 cells visited.
No halt in the accelerated simulator (tool not verified; 20 checkpoints against the plain one).
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).
Crossing the background words, proved for every length.
The local pattern every halt must pass through.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.471). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.505).
After 109 steps the tape spans 46,120 cells (20,785 left of the start, 12,876 right), with a density of 1s of 0.6.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Sweeps that rewrite a periodic tape
html: <div class="col">

The head sweeps right and left, turning wherever the local pattern sends it back, and every sweep rewrites what it crosses. Rightward (D and E, with F and A) the tape is put into a rightward form: D turns each 011 into 100 and each 01 into 11, E turns 110 into 001 and 10 into 11, and a period-12 word such as 101101011010 becomes 110011100111. Leftward (C with D, A, B making small zigzags) the tape goes back to its leftward form.

Seen at the left end the tape is a clean zone (011)a (or (101)a), then a block of the period-12 word (101011010110)B that grows by one copy per visit of the left end, then one or two more huge blocks of longer words and a short tail such as (10)a 1 (10)b 1 and (110)3 (10)3, where the irregular events happen. The clean zone does not grow: it shrinks at each conversion of the left block. In the rightward form the soup reads as runs of 1s separated by 0 0.

sections.heading: What one sweep does to the words it crosses
html: A shift rule says that a sweep crosses any number n of copies of a word in one state and leaves n copies of another word behind. These are proved in Lean for every n and every tape around them (lean/Rules.lean); S> is the head in state S on the next cell, L and R the rest of the tape.

sections.heading: A few huge blocks and a short tail
html: <div class="col">
Look at the tape each time state A arrives at the left end. It is a short clean zone, a huge block of one 12-cell word, some junk, a second huge block of a longer word, and a short tail:

Every visit adds one word to the left block; the tail, a small engine of at most about 200 cells, eats the block (U)^C. This is the shape of two machines of this group that have been settled (two blocks and a tail from a finite set), and part of the same method works here.

From 2.5·108 to 2.3·109 steps the tail right of the block (101010101101101)^C takes exactly 118 values and repeats every 118 visits of the left end (5,250 re-occurrences in the plain run); per cycle B + 118 and C − 25. The symbolic simulator proves it as a rule with all three counts free: (a, B, C) = (42 + 3x0, 748 + 3x1, 190 + 3x2) goes to (a, B + 354, C − 75) in 708 events.

The method does not finish the job, for four reasons. When a block is used up another phase starts with another word, sometimes with three big blocks. Some phases build a row of blocks (10)^k in which each block is twice as long as the one before, so the number of blocks grows (slowly) with the tape. The clean zone at the left end is a third counter that shrinks whenever the left block is converted. And in some phases the tail does not repeat at all.

sections.heading: The one pattern that halts, and why it has not appeared
html: <div class="col">

The machine halts only when B reads a 1, and Lean proves that the only way there is D reading 0 0 0 1 (D, E and A each write a 1 and step right, and B meets the 1; halt_needs_pattern, lean/Halt.lean). In the first 109 steps D read 0 0 0 6,026 times, every one on blank cells past the right end of the tape, never inside it.
Inside the tape, separators of two 0s are common in the rightward form, so a third 0 next to them is the danger. The run never produced one in 109 steps, but no invariant that forbids it is known.

Next step. Write the soup as a sequence of blocks (the runs between 00 separators) and find the block rewriting done by one round trip; then look for an invariant on blocks that keeps separators at most two 0s wide.

Twin. 1RB1RE_1RC0RF_0LD---_1LE1LD_1RA0LB_0RE1RF is this table with the states renamed (A→B, B→C, C→D, D→E, E→A, F→F); it starts in the state this machine calls E. The two runs from blank tape are different (no common configuration at the left end in their first 300,000 steps), but they use the same sweeps, words and halting pattern, and every rule here holds there after renaming.
